check.question: Which ticket IDs were open or pending at the end of March 31, 2026?
check.sql:
SELECT t.ticket_id
FROM tickets AS t
WHERE t.created_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
  AND (
    SELECT s.to_status
    FROM ticket_events AS e
    JOIN ticket_status_events AS s ON s.event_id = e.event_id
    WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
      AND e.occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
    ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) IN ('open', 'pending')
ORDER BY t.ticket_id;
check.wrong_sql:
SELECT t.ticket_id
FROM tickets AS t
WHERE t.created_at <= '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
  AND (
    SELECT s.to_status
    FROM ticket_events AS e
    JOIN ticket_status_events AS s ON s.event_id = e.event_id
    WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
      AND e.occurred_at <= '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
    ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) IN ('open', 'pending')
ORDER BY t.ticket_id;
check.witness: Frozen-fixture fact that separates gold from wrong: event 103 / ticket_status_events 103 moves ticket 1 from pending to closed at exactly 2026-04-01 00:00:00, and the March cutoff is exclusive (occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'), so ticket 1 must still be pending in the March snapshot. The wrong query replays events with an inclusive cutoff (shipping assumption: the April 1 midnight boundary belongs to March), which applies event 103 and drops ticket 1, yielding rows 2-19 instead of 1-19. Hand-derived gold replay (order by occurred_at, seq): ticket 1 -> pending (event 102 applies; event 103 excluded); ticket 2 -> open (its three 2026-04-01 00:00:00 events 202/203/204 are all excluded); ticket 3 -> open (302 close, 303/305 reopens; seq 5 wins the same-timestamp tie); tickets 4-19 -> open via their created events (messages carry no status). All 19 fixture tickets were created 2026-02-01 00:00:00, before the cutoff, so none are absent. Derived by hand from the frozen fixture as printed; this review environment exposes no shell/SQLite binary, so rows are literal hand derivations cross-checked against the fixture insert ledger, not pasted query output.
